Pathland — Session Context (for new sessions)
Project
Rust retained-mode UI runtime; SwiftUI-like declarative DSL; 16-byte opcode protocol. Protocol-first, renderers stateless, native elements everywhere.
Architecture decisions (already implemented & tested — 69 tests green, GTK + Java demos run)
- WIT world (wit/pathland.wit) = canonical flat, id-based cross-language surface (builder/engine/input/app, variants), no per-component wrappers.
- Native (non-WASM) path: pathland-native is a cdylib exposing the flat world as pathland_native_* C functions over a zero-copy shared-memory ring. Swift/Java/C# link it via FFI, call the flat surface, and read opcodes zero-copy (no serialization, no WASM on desktop).
- WASM is browser-only: pathland-guest (wasm component) for CSR worker / optional SSR; pathland-wit-host (wasmtime) for remote hosts.
- Frame type = the transport seam: a driver consumes Frames regardless of origin (shared ring, decoded batch).
- pathland-transport: RingTransport (zero-copy SPSC), FrameSource/DriverTransport/InputSink/TransportError/OpcodeBatch, NetBatchEncoder (remote). pathland-guest wasm component built via cargo component.
- Fixed a header wire bug: shared-memory header offsets were overlapping (OFF_ARENA_BYTES=0x14 overlapped OFF_ARENA_OFFSET=0x12). Corrected to: arenaBytes=0x16, arenaCursor=0x1A, readCursor=0x1E, writeCursor=0x22, frameCount=0x26 in pathland-opcode/src/memory.rs + spec/OPCODE.md + Java RingReader. Native worked (uses layout, not header fields); foreign zero-copy drivers were broken.
- Demos: pathland-gtk-demo (Rust GTK, native shared ring), lib/java/pathland-demo (Maven + JNA + SwiftUI-like Java DSL, zero-copy ring read).
Current task (IN PROGRESS, next steps): Catalog-Driven DSL + Frame modifier
Goal
Generate the SwiftUI-like DSL from a single YAML catalog — define a core component once, get the ergonomic DSL in any language (starting with Java), no hand-written per-component classes.
New files
- lib/ui/components.yaml — single source of truth for the DSL (components, per-component constructor properties, global modifiers, enum values, ids).
- pathland-codegen — a Rust bin crate that parses YAML (serde_yaml), asserts every id against pathland_opcode::constants (hard build error on mismatch — the consistency safety net), and emits checked-in Java DSL.
- generate.sh / cargo run -p pathland-codegen to regenerate + re-run conformance.
Generated Java (checked-in)
Constants.java, typed enum classes (Align, Justify, TextAlign, Truncation, FontWeight), View.java (interface + simple modifiers + frame), ComponentNode.java, DSL.java, Modified.java (extended for compound frame). Keep Node/Bridge/RingReader/PathlandNative static.
Confirmed DSL rules (NON-NEGOTIABLE)
- Component construction properties: structural/layout, per-component, constructor args, NO chaining.
- stacks (hstack/vstack): alignment, justification, spacing
- text: text_alignment, line_limit, truncation_mode
- Global modifiers: appearance/decoration, chainable on any view: padding, color, background_color, opacity, border_width, border_color, border_radius, font_size, font_weight, font_family, visible, z_index, clips_to_bounds.
- spacing = property (constructor); padding = modifier (always). Any code treating them otherwise is a bug.
- No standalone width/height. Instead frame compound modifier: .frame(width, height, alignment) — reuses ALIGNMENT (0x0002); no .width()/.height() sugar. Sentinels FILL = -1.0, HUG_CONTENT = -2.0 exposed as Frame.FILL/Frame.HUG_CONTENT.
- Typed Java enums, not raw ints (e.g. .alignment(Align.CENTER)).
- Ids live in YAML; Rust generator asserts each against constants.rs.
Rust DSL change (breaking — do it now)
- Remove Node.width / Node.height fields from pathland_view::Node.
- Add a Frame modifier (view-modifier capturing width/height/alignment) that emits WIDTH/HEIGHT (+ ALIGNMENT when set) as ordinary SET_PROPERTY.
- Refactor pathland-engine emit_size_props and the WIDTH/HEIGHT diff logic into ordinary property diffs.
- Update pathland-gtk-demo to use .frame(...); migrate affected tests.
Enum values
- Align (stack/container cross-axis): leading, center, trailing, fill
- Justify (main-axis): start, end, center, space_between, space_around, space_evenly
- TextAlign: leading, center, trailing
- Truncation: head, middle, tail, none
- FontWeight: light, regular, medium, semibold, bold
Component ids (from constants.rs)
hstack=0x0001, vstack=0x0002, text=0x0003, button=0x0004, image=0x0005, switch=0x0006, text_field=0x0007, spacer=0x0008, scrollview=0x0009, list=0x000A, grid=0x000B, comment=0x000C
Property ids (from constants.rs)
spacing=0x0001, alignment=0x0002, justification=0x0003, padding=0x0004, content_margins=0x0005, text=0x000A, line_limit=0x000B, text_alignment=0x000C, truncation_mode=0x000D, background_color=0x1001, border_width=0x1003, border_color=0x1004, border_radius=0x1005, padding_style=0x1006, font_size=0x1007, font_weight=0x1008, font_family=0x1009, color=0x100A, width=0x100B, height=0x100C, opacity=0x100D, visible=0x100E, z_index=0x100F, clips_to_bounds=0x1010, padding_top/right/bottom/left=0x1012-0x1015, role=0x2001, state=0x2002, enabled=0x2003, selected=0x2004
Phases
- A — YAML catalog + Rust generator + generated Java DSL (checked-in) + id assertions.
- B — Rust DSL frame modifier; remove Node.width/height; refactor engine; update GTK demo + tests.
- C — Verify: cargo test, generator assertions, Java headless (DemoHeadless) + Swing (DemoApp) demo run.
Helpful run commands
- Rust tests: cd lib/rust && PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo test
- GTK demo: cd lib/rust && PATH="$HOME/.cargo/bin:$PATH" cargo run -p pathland-gtk-demo
- Java demo: cargo build -p pathland-native then cd lib/java/pathland-demo && mvn -q -Dpathland.rust.target=<lib/rust/target/debug> compile exec:java
- Java headless verify: mvn ... -Dexec.mainClass=demo.DemoHeadless compile exec:java (expect OK: Java DSL -> Rust engine -> shared ring -> zero-copy read = 'Count: 8')
I'll explore the current state of the repo to figure out where things stand across the three phases.

1: //! # pathland-view
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland SwiftUI-style view DSL. Core components (`VStack`, `HStack`,
4: //! `Text`) and chainable modifiers (`spacing`, `padding`, `font_size`, `color`,
5: //! `background`) build a retained **view tree** (`Node`) that
6: //! `pathland-engine` turns into declarative `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes.
7: //!
8: //! ## Building a tree
9: //!
10: //! Use the `vstack!`/`hstack!` macros (which box children for you) with the
11: //! free `text`/`spacer` functions, then chain modifiers and `build()`:
12: //!
13: //! ```
14: //! use pathland_view::{vstack, hstack, text, View, ViewExt};
15: //!
16: //! let node = vstack![
17: //!     text("a"),
18: //!     hstack![text("b")],
19: //! ]
20: //! .padding(16.0)
21: //! .build();
22: //! # let _ = node;
23: //! ```
24: //!
25: //! ## Decoupled modifiers
26: //!
27: //! Modifiers are **decoupled from views** (SwiftUI-style): any modifier applies
28: //! to any view via the blanket `View::modifier`, and application code composes
29: //! **custom modifiers** from the core ones by implementing `ViewModifier`:
30: //!
31: //! ```
32: //! use pathland_view::{View, ViewExt, ViewModifier, Node, Padding, Background};
33: //!
34: //! struct Card;
35: //! impl ViewModifier for Card {
36: //!     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node) {
37: //!         Padding(16.0).apply(node);
38: //!         Background(0xFF_EEEEEE).apply(node);
39: //!     }
40: //! }
41: //!
42: //! // Works on any view:
43: //! let a = pathland_view::text("A").modifier(Card);
44: //! let b = pathland_view::vstack![].modifier(Card);
45: //! # let _ = (a, b);
46: //! ```
47: //!
48: //! Unsupported combinations are **allowed and ignored**: the modifier emits its
49: //! property and the renderer ignores what it cannot apply.
50: //!
51: //! ## No layout math
52: //!
53: //! The DSL describes structure + constraint properties only. It never computes
54: //! bounds; native renderers lay out their own elements.
55: //!
56: //! This crate is `no_std` + `alloc`.
57: 
58: #![no_std]
59: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]
60: 
61: #[cfg(test)]

63: 
64: extern crate alloc;
65: 
66: use alloc::collections::BTreeMap;
67: use alloc::string::String;
68: use alloc::vec::Vec;

70: /// Re-exported for `vstack!`/`hstack!` macro hygiene (`$crate::Box`).
71: pub use alloc::boxed::Box;
72: /// Re-exported for `vstack!`/`hstack!` macro hygiene (`$crate::vec!`).
73: pub use alloc::vec;

75: use pathland_opcode::component_type;
76: use pathland_opcode::property_id;

78: pub use pathland_opcode;

80: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
81: // Core component macros + free functions
82: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

84: /// Build a vertical stack from a comma-separated list of views.
85: ///
86: /// Each child is boxed automatically, so children can mix `Text`, `HStack`,
87: /// modified views, or custom `View` implementations. Nested stacks work:
88: ///
89: /// ```
90: /// use pathland_view::{vstack, text, View};
91: /// let node = vstack![text("a"), text("b")].build();
92: /// # let _ = node;
93: /// ```
94: #[macro_export]
95: macro_rules! vstack {
96:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
97:         $crate::VStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
98:     };
99: }
100: 
101: /// Build a horizontal stack from a comma-separated list of views.
102: ///
103: /// See [`vstack!`] for details.
104: #[macro_export]
105: macro_rules! hstack {
106:     ($($child:expr),* $(,)?) => {
107:         $crate::HStack::new().children($crate::vec![$($crate::Box::new($child)),*])
108:     };
109: }

111: /// A text view from a string literal (shorthand for [`Text::new`]).
112: pub fn text(content: &str) -> Text {
113:     Text::new(content)
114: }

125: /// A node in the retained view tree (the application's canonical UI tree).
126: #[derive(Clone, PartialEq)]
127: pub struct Node {
128:     /// Stable node id (0 until `assign_ids`).

130:     pub component: Component,
131:     pub children: Vec<Node>,

174:     /// Horizontal stack (native horizontal container).
175:     HStack,
176:     /// Text leaf.

178:     /// Interactive button.

184: impl core::fmt::Debug for Component {
185:     fn fmt(&self, f: &mut core::fmt::Formatter<'_>) -> core::fmt::Result {
186:         match self {
187:             Component::VStack => f.write_str("VStack"),
188:             Component::HStack => f.write_str("HStack"),
189:             Component::Text { text } => f.debug_tuple("Text").field(text).finish(),
190:             Component::Button { label } => f.debug_tuple("Button").field(label).finish(),
191:             Component::Spacer => f.write_str("Spacer"),

193:     }
194: }

196: /// Map a component to its protocol component type id.
197: pub fn component_type_id(component: &Component) -> u16 {
198:     match component {
199:         Component::VStack => component_type::VSTACK,
200:         Component::HStack => component_type::HSTACK,
201:         Component::Text { .. } => component_type::TEXT,
202:         Component::Button { .. } => component_type::BUTTON,
203:         Component::Spacer => component_type::SPACER,
204:     }
205: }

207: /// The protocol value type for a property id.
208: ///
209: /// Color-valued properties (COLOR, BACKGROUND_COLOR, …) are emitted with the
210: /// `COLOR` value type; all other constraint/style properties are `F32`.
211: pub fn value_type_for(prop: u16) -> u8 {
212:     match prop {
213:         property_id::COLOR
214:         | property_id::BACKGROUND_COLOR
215:         | property_id::BORDER_COLOR => pathland_opcode::value_type::COLOR,
216:         _ => pathland_opcode::value_type::F32,
217:     }
218: }

221: // View protocol
222: // ---------------------------------------------------------------------------

224: /// A composable view. Implement for custom views; the core components and
225: /// `Modified` wrappers implement it already.
226: pub trait View {
227:     /// Build the retained node for this view.
228:     fn build(&self) -> Node;
229: }

231: /// A view decorator (SwiftUI `ViewModifier`): transforms a node's properties.
232: ///
233: /// Core modifiers (`Spacing`, `Padding`, `FontSize`, `Color`, `Background`)
234: /// implement this; application code implements it to compose custom modifiers.
235: pub trait ViewModifier {
236:     /// Apply the modifier to `node` (mutating constraint properties).
237:     fn apply(&self, node: &mut Node);
238: }

241: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
242: pub struct Modified<V, M> {
243:     view: V,
244:     modifier: M,
245: }

247: impl<V: View, M: ViewModifier> View for Modified<V, M> {
248:     fn build(&self) -> Node {
249:         let mut node = self.view.build();

1: //! # pathland-engine
2: //!
3: //! The Pathland **guest engine**. It holds the application's **retained view
4: //! tree** (built with the SwiftUI-style DSL in `pathland-view`) and emits the
5: //! **declarative structure** as `TREE`/`STYLE` opcodes into the 16-byte ring
6: //! buffer — VStack, HStack, Text, spacing, padding, alignment. It does **not**
7: //! compute rects or layout; native renderers (GTK4 widgets, DOM flexbox) lay
8: //! out their own native elements from these constraints.
9: //!
10: //! ## Reactive emission
11: //!
12: //! Emission is **diff-based**: on each `emit` the engine compares the current
13: //! tree against a snapshot of what it last emitted, and writes only the
14: //! opcodes for nodes that actually changed. An unchanged tree emits **zero**
15: //! opcodes. This is what signals in the application drive — a signal marks the
16: //! tree dirty; `emit` reconciles.
17: //!
18: //! Both **property diffs** (`SET_PROPERTY`, `SET_TEXT`) and **structural diffs**
19: //! (`CREATE_NODE`, `DELETE_NODE`, `INSERT_CHILD`, `REMOVE_CHILD`, `MOVE_CHILD`)
20: //! are emitted.
21: //!
22: //! ## Zero allocation
23: //!
24: //! The emit pass performs **zero dynamic heap allocations** in the steady
25: //! state. The snapshot is a preallocated slab indexed by node id; per-pass
26: //! bookkeeping uses generation stamps instead of rebuilding maps. Allocations
27: //! only occur when the tree *grows* (new nodes resize the slab) or a node's
28: //! property set actually changes.
29:

31: #![forbid(unsafe_op_in_unsafe_fn)]

84: /// The diff-based reactive emitter.
85: ///
86: /// `Engine` keeps the snapshot of what was last emitted. Calling `emit` with a
87: /// (possibly mutated) retained tree writes only the delta opcodes. The steady
88: /// state of the emit pass allocates nothing.
89: pub struct Engine {
90:     /// nodeId → last emitted state (a preallocated slab; node ids are dense).
91:     snapshot: Vec<Option<SnapshotNode>>,
92:     /// Monotonic generation stamp for the current pass.

103:     pub fn new() -> Self {
104:         Self {
105:             snapshot: Vec::new(),

107:         }
108:     }

110:     /// Reconcile `root` against the snapshot, emitting only changed opcodes.
111:     pub fn emit(
112:         &mut self,
113:         root: &Node,
114:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
115:     ) -> Result<EmitResult, pathland_opcode::RingError> {
116:         self.gen = self.gen.wrapping_add(1);
117:         let mut out = 0usize;
118:         self.reconcile_node(root, None, 0, guest, &mut out)?;
119: 
120:         // Delete any node that existed in the snapshot but was not visited this
121:         // pass (generation stamp unchanged).
122:         for (id, slot) in self.snapshot.iter_mut().enumerate() {
123:             if let Some(s) = slot {
124:                 if s.gen != self.gen {
125:                     guest.delete_node(id as u32)?;
126:                     out += 1;

148:     fn reconcile_node(
149:         &mut self,
150:         node: &Node,
151:         parent: Option<u32>,
152:         index: usize,
153:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
154:         out: &mut usize,
155:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_opcode::RingError> {
156:         let component_type = component_type_id(&node.component);
157: 
158:         let text_borrowed = match &node.component {
159:             Component::Text { text } => Some(text.as_str()),
160:             Component::Button { label } => Some(label.as_str()),
161:             _ => None,
162:         };
163: 
164:         let prev = self.slot_mut(node.id).take();
165:         let props_changed = match &prev {
166:             Some(p) => p.properties != node.properties,
167:             None => !node.properties.is_empty(),
168:         };
169:         // Text is owned in the snapshot; compare without cloning.
170:         let text_changed = match &prev {
171:             Some(p) => p.text.as_deref() != text_borrowed,
172:             None => text_borrowed.is_some(),
173:         };
174: 
175:         match &prev {
176:             // New node: CREATE_NODE + INSERT_CHILD + all properties/text.
177:             None => {
178:                 guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
179:                 *out += 1;
180:                 if let Some(p) = parent {
181:                     guest.insert_child(p, node.id, index as u32)?;
182:                     *out += 1;
183:                 }
184:                 for (prop, value) in &node.properties {
185:                     guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
186:                     *out += 1;
187:                 }
188:                 self.emit_size_props(node, guest, out)?;
189:                 if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
190:                     guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
191:                     *out += 1;
192:                 }
193:             }
194:             Some(p) => {
195:                 // Structural changes.
196:                 if p.parent != parent {
197:                     if let Some(old) = p.parent {
198:                         guest.remove_child(old, node.id)?;
199:                         *out += 1;
200:                     }
201:                     if let Some(new) = parent {
202:                         guest.insert_child(new, node.id, index as u32)?;
203:                         *out += 1;
204:                     }
205:                 } else if p.index != index {
206:                     if let Some(par) = parent {
207:                         guest.move_child(par, node.id, index as u32)?;
208:                         *out += 1;
209:                     }
210:                 }
211:                 // Component type changed → recreate.
212:                 if p.component_type != component_type {
213:                     guest.create_node(node.id, component_type)?;
214:                     *out += 1;
215:                 }
216:                 // Text diff.
217:                 if text_changed {
218:                     if let Some(t) = text_borrowed {
219:                         guest.set_text(node.id, t)?;
220:                         *out += 1;
221:                     }
222:                 }
223:                 // Size modifier diffs (WIDTH/HEIGHT).
224:                 if p.width != node.width {
225:                     if let Some(w) = node.width {
226:                         guest.set_property(
227:                             node.id,
228:                             pathland_opcode::property_id::WIDTH,
229:                             value_type::F32,
230:                             w.to_bits(),
231:                         )?;
232:                         *out += 1;
233:                     }
234:                 }
235:                 if p.height != node.height {
236:                     if let Some(h) = node.height {
237:                         guest.set_property(
238:                             node.id,
239:                             pathland_opcode::property_id::HEIGHT,
240:                             value_type::F32,
241:                             h.to_bits(),
242:                         )?;
243:                         *out += 1;
244:                     }
245:                 }
246:                 // Generic property diffs (new or changed values only). This
247:                 // covers stack spacing/padding, fonts, colors, and any modifier
248:                 // applied to the node.
249:                 for (prop, value) in &node.properties {
250:                     if p.properties.get(prop) != Some(value) {
251:                         guest.set_property(node.id, *prop, value_type_for(*prop), *value)?;
252:                         *out += 1;
253:                     }
254:                 }
255:             }
256:         }
257: 
258:         // Store the current state for the next pass. When the property map and
259:         // text are unchanged, move the previous allocations back so the steady
260:         // state allocates nothing; otherwise build fresh values.
261:         let mut prev_props = None;
262:         let mut prev_text = None;
263:         if let Some(p) = prev {
264:             if !props_changed {
265:                 prev_props = Some(p.properties);
266:             }
267:             if !text_changed {
268:                 prev_text = p.text;
269:             }
270:             // If both moved out, `p` is fully consumed.
271:             let _ = p;
272:         }
273:         let properties = match prev_props {
274:             Some(props) => props,
275:             None => node.properties.clone(),
276:         };
277:         let text = match prev_text {
278:             Some(t) => Some(t),
279:             None => text_borrowed.map(|s| s.to_owned()),
280:         };
281:         *self.slot_mut(node.id) = Some(SnapshotNode {
282:             component_type,
283:             parent,
284:             index,
285:             text,
286:             width: node.width,
287:             height: node.height,
288:             properties,
289:             gen: self.gen,
290:         });
291: 
292:         for (i, child) in node.children.iter().enumerate() {
293:             self.reconcile_node(child, Some(node.id), i, guest, out)?;
294:         }
295:         Ok(())
296:     }

301:         node: &Node,
302:         guest: &mut Guest<'_>,
303:         out: &mut usize,
304:     ) -> Result<(), pathland_opcode::RingError> {

1: //! # Pathland GTK4 desktop demo
2: //!
3: //! A native GTK4 app demonstrating Pathland's **zero-copy shared-memory ring**.
4: //!
5: //! The developer authors the UI with the SwiftUI-style DSL; the native
6: //! `pathland_engine` emits declarative 16-byte opcodes into a shared linear
7: //! memory ring (`RingTransport`). The driver reads completed frames back from
8: //! the same ring — no serialization, no batching, no copies — and renders to
9: //! native GTK widgets.
10: //!
11: //! This is the local/desktop transport: producer (engine) and consumer (driver)
12: //! share one address space. Remote rendering (WebSocket/batch) is a separate
13: //! transport used by SSR — see `pathland-transport`.
14: 
15: use std::cell::RefCell;
16: use std::rc::Rc;
17: 
18: use gtk::prelude::*;
19: use gtk::{Align, Application, ApplicationWindow, Box as GtkBox, Label, Orientation};
20: use pathland_engine::Engine;
21: use pathland_host::RenderTree;
22: use pathland_transport::{FrameSource, RingTransport};
23: use pathland_view::{assign_ids, button, hstack, text, vstack, Node, View, ViewExt};
24: 
25: const APP_ID: &str = "org.pathland.GtkDemo";
26: 
27: /// Build the DSL tree for the current counter value. This is the developer's
28: /// authoring surface.
29: fn build_tree(count: u32) -> Node {
30:     vstack![
31:         hstack![
32:             text(format!("Count: {}", count).as_str()),
33:             button("Increment"),
34:         ]
35:         .padding(16.0),
36:         text("Pathland · GTK4 · shared ring").color(0xFF_888888),
37:     ]
38:     .padding(24.0)
39:     .build()
40: }
41: 
42: /// Demo state: the diff-based engine + the shared ring it writes into.
43: struct Demo {
44:     engine: Engine,
45:     ring: RingTransport,
46:     count: u32,
47:     /// Button-click callback (set once during UI setup).
48:     on_click: Option<Rc<dyn Fn()>>,
49: }
50: 
51: fn main() {
52:     let app = Application::builder().application_id(APP_ID).build();
53:     app.connect_activate(build_ui);
54:     app.run();
55: }
56: 
57: fn build_ui(app: &Application) {
58:     // Shared app state (mutable through Rc<RefCell> across callbacks).
59:     let demo = Rc::new(RefCell::new(Demo {
60:         engine: Engine::new(),
61:         ring: RingTransport::new(),
62:         count: 0,
63:         on_click: None,
64:     }));
65: 
66:     let window = ApplicationWindow::builder()
67:         .application(app)
68:         .title("Pathland GTK4 Demo")
69:         .default_width(420)
70:         .default_height(220)
71:         .build();
72: 
73:     let root = GtkBox::new(Orientation::Vertical, 0);
74:     window.set_child(Some(&root));
75: 
76:     // Initial render through the shared ring.
77:     let demo_ren = Rc::clone(&demo);
78:     let root_ren = root.clone();
79:     let re_render = move || render(&demo_ren, &root_ren);
80:     re_render();
81: 
82:     // Button click: apply state change, then re-render through the ring.
83:     let demo_click = Rc::clone(&demo);
84:     let root_click = root.clone();
85:     let on_click: Rc<dyn Fn()> = Rc::new(move || {
86:         let mut d = demo_click.borrow_mut();
87:         d.count = d.count.wrapping_add(1);
88:         drop(d);
89:         render(&demo_click, &root_click);
90:     });
91:     demo.borrow_mut().on_click = Some(on_click);
92: 
93:     window.present();
94: }
95: 
96: /// Pipeline: DSL -> engine -> shared ring -> RenderTree -> GTK widgets.
97: ///
98: /// The engine writes opcodes into the ring's producer view; the driver reads
99: /// the completed frame from the same ring via `FrameSource`. Zero-copy.
100: fn render(demo: &Rc<RefCell<Demo>>, root: &GtkBox) {
101:     let mut d = demo.borrow_mut();
102:     let on_click: Option<Rc<dyn Fn()>> = d.on_click.clone();
103:     let mut tree = build_tree(d.count);
104:     assign_ids(&mut tree, &mut 1);
105: 
106:     // Disjoint field borrows: engine (producer state) and ring (transport).
107:     let Demo {
108:         engine,
109:         ring,
110:         count: _,
111:         on_click: _,
112:     } = &mut *d;
113: 
114:     // 1. Producer writes opcodes into the shared ring.
115:     {
116:         let mut guest = ring.producer();
117:         guest.begin_frame();
118:         engine.emit(&tree, &mut guest).ok();
119:         guest.end_frame();
120:     }
121: 
122:     // 2. Consumer reads the completed frame from the same ring.
123:     let frame = ring.next_frame().ok().flatten().expect("a frame after emit");
124:     let frame = frame.frame();
125: 
126:     // 3. Apply the frame to the native-element description.
127:     let mut render = RenderTree::default();
128:     render.apply_frame(frame);
129: 
130:     // 4. Rebuild the GTK widget hierarchy.
131:     while let Some(child) = root.first_child() {
132:         root.remove(&child);
133:     }
134:     if let Some(root_node_id) = render.root().map(|n| n.id) {
135:         root.append(&render_node(&render, root_node_id, on_click));
136:     }
137:     root.show();
138: }
139: 
140: /// Build a GTK widget subtree for a node id from the `RenderTree`.
141: fn render_node(render: &RenderTree, id: u32, on_click: Option<Rc<dyn Fn()>>) -> gtk::Widget {
142:     let node = render.node(id).unwrap();
143:     match node.component_type {
144:         pathland_opcode::component_type::VSTACK => {
145:             let bx = GtkBox::new(Orientation::Vertical, spacing(render, id));
146:             bx.set_halign(Align::Fill);
147:             bx.set_valign(Align::Fill);
148:             for child in &node.children {
149:                 bx.append(&render_node(render, *child, on_click.clone()));
150:             }
151:             bx.upcast()
152:         }
153:         pathland_opcode::component_type::HSTACK => {
154:             let bx = GtkBox::new(Orientation::Horizontal, spacing(render, id));
155:             bx.set_halign(Align::Center);
156:             bx.set_valign(Align::Center);
157:             for child in &node.children {
158:                 bx.append(&render_node(render, *child, on_click.clone()));
159:             }
160:             bx.upcast()
161:         }
162:         pathland_opcode::component_type::TEXT => {
163:             let label = Label::new(Some(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or("")));
164:             apply_text_style(&label, render, id);
165:             label.upcast()
166:         }
167:         pathland_opcode::component_type::BUTTON => {
168:             let btn = gtk::Button::with_label(node.text.as_deref().unwrap_or(""));
169:             if let Some(cb) = on_click {
170:                 btn.connect_clicked(move |_| cb());
171:             }
172:             btn.upcast()
173:         }
174:         _ => Label::new(Some("")).upcast(),
175:     }
176: }
177: 
178: /// Spacing property value for a node (default 4).
179: fn spacing(render: &RenderTree, id: u32) -> i32 {
180:     render
181:         .node(id)
182:         .and_then(|n| n.properties.get(&pathland_opcode::property_id::SPACING))
183:         .map(|b| f32::from_bits(*b) as i32)
184:         .unwrap_or(4)
185: }
186: 
187: /// Apply color/font-size text style from properties via Pango attributes.
188: fn apply_text_style(label: &Label, render: &RenderTree, id: u32) {
189:     let node = render.node(id).unwrap();
190:     let attrs = pango::AttrList::new();
191:     if let Some(fs) = node.properties.get(&pathland_opcode::property_id::FONT_SIZE) {
192:         // Font size is stored in points (f32); pango scales points to device units.
193:         let pts = (f32::from_bits(*fs).max(0.0) as i32) * 1000;
194:         attrs.insert(pango::AttrSize::new(pts));
195:     }
196:     if let Some(color) = node.properties.get(&pathland_opcode::property_id::COLOR) {
197:         let c = *color;
198:         let red = (((c >> 16) & 0xFF) as u16) * 257;
199:         let green = (((c >> 8) & 0xFF) as u16) * 257;
200:         let blue = ((c & 0xFF) as u16) * 257;
201:         let mut fg = pango::AttrColor::new_foreground(red, green, blue);
202:         fg.set_start_index(0);
203:         fg.set_end_index(u32::MAX);
204:         attrs.insert(fg);
205:     }
206:     label.set_attributes(Some(&attrs));
207: }

1: //! # pathland-native
2: //!
3: //! Native (non-WASM) projection of the Pathland flat world, exposed over both a
4: //! Rust API and a C ABI for foreign host languages (Swift / Java / C# / …).
5: //!
6: //! This is the **cross-language, zero-copy** path: a host links this crate as a
7: //! native library (or a `cdylib` and its `pathland_native_*` C functions), drives
8: //! the retained tree with the flat `builder`/`engine` operations, and reads
9: //! opcodes from the **shared-memory ring in place** — no serialization, no batch,
10: //! no WASM.
11: //!
12: //! The surface mirrors `wit/pathland.wit` (`builder`, `engine`) but for a native
13: //! shared-memory transport instead of a WASM/WIT ABI.
14: 
15: use std::collections::{BTreeMap, HashMap};
16: 
17: use pathland_engine::Engine;
18: use pathland_opcode::{component_type, property_id, MemoryLayout};
19: use pathland_transport::RingTransport;
20: use pathland_view::{component_type_id, Node};
21: 
22: mod capi;
23: 
24: /// A flat node in the host's retained tree (id → node).
25: #[derive(Clone)]
26: pub struct FlatNode {
27:     pub id: u32,
28:     pub view_component: pathland_view::Component,
29:     pub properties: BTreeMap<u16, u32>,
30:     pub parent: Option<u32>,
31:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
32: }
33: 
34: /// The native host: owns the retained tree, the diff engine, and the shared
35: /// zero-copy ring.
36: pub struct NativeHost {
37:     nodes: HashMap<u32, FlatNode>,
38:     engine: Engine,
39:     ring: RingTransport,
40: }
41: 
42: /// Safe, checked operations returning `()` (used by the C shim).
43: #[derive(Debug, Clone, Copy, PartialEq, Eq)]
44: pub enum HostError {
45:     /// The operation referenced a missing node.
46:     NotFound,
47: }
48: 
49: impl NativeHost {
50:     /// Create a host with a fresh shared ring (default layout).
51:     pub fn new() -> Self {
52:         Self {
53:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
54:             engine: Engine::new(),
55:             ring: RingTransport::new(),
56:         }
57:     }
58: 
59:     /// Create a host over a caller-provided ring buffer + layout.
60:     pub fn with_buffer(mem: Vec<u8>, layout: MemoryLayout) -> Self {
61:         Self {
62:             nodes: HashMap::new(),
63:             engine: Engine::new(),
64:             ring: RingTransport::with_buffer(mem, layout),
65:         }
66:     }
67: 
68:     /// Create (or reset) a node with a host-supplied stable id.
69:     pub fn create_node(&mut self, id: u32, component: pathland_view::Component) {
70:         let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_insert(FlatNode {
71:             id,
72:             view_component: component.clone(),
73:             properties: BTreeMap::new(),
74:             parent: None,
75:             children: Vec::new(),
76:         });
77:         entry.view_component = component;
78:         entry.properties.clear();
79:     }
80: 
81:     /// Insert `child` into `parent` at `index` (u32::MAX appends).
82:     pub fn insert_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32, index: u32) {
83:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
84:             let idx = if index == u32::MAX {
85:                 p.children.len()
86:             } else {
87:                 (index as usize).min(p.children.len())
88:             };
89:             if !p.children.contains(&child) {
90:                 p.children.insert(idx, child);
91:             }
92:         }
93:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
94:             c.parent = Some(parent);
95:         }
96:     }
97: 
98:     /// Remove `child` from `parent`.
99:     pub fn remove_child(&mut self, parent: u32, child: u32) {
100:         if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
101:             p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
102:         }
103:         if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
104:             c.parent = None;
105:         }
106:     }
107: 
108:     /// Set a node's text content.
109:     pub fn set_text(&mut self, id: u32, text: &str) {
110:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
111:             match &mut node.view_component {
112:                 pathland_view::Component::Text { text: t } => *t = text.into(),
113:                 pathland_view::Component::Button { label } => *label = text.into(),
114:                 _ => {}
115:             }
116:         }
117:     }
118: 
119:     /// Set a constraint/style property (raw value bits; valueType derived from
120:     /// the property id).
121:     pub fn set_property(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, value: u32) {
122:         if let Some(node) = self.nodes.get_mut(&id) {
123:             node.properties.insert(prop, value);
124:         }
125:     }
126: 
127:     /// Set a float property (stores `f32` bit pattern).
128:     pub fn set_property_f32(&mut self, id: u32, prop: u16, value: f32) {
129:         self.set_property(id, prop, value.to_bits());
130:     }
131: 
132:     /// Emit the retained tree as opcodes into the shared ring.
133:     ///
134:     /// Returns `true` if a frame was written (i.e. the tree is non-empty).
135:     pub fn emit(&mut self) -> bool {
136:         let root = self.root_id().and_then(|r| self.materialize(r));
137:         if let Some(root) = root {
138:             let mut guest = self.ring.producer();
139:             guest.begin_frame();
140:             let _ = self.engine.emit(&root, &mut guest);
141:             guest.end_frame();
142:             true
143:         } else {
144:             false
145:         }
146:     }
147: 
148:     /// The ring's linear-memory buffer (for embedding / FFI).
149:     pub fn ring_buffer(&self) -> &[u8] {
150:         self.ring.buffer()
151:     }
152: 
153:     /// Consume the ring transport (for hosts that read frames via `FrameSource`).
154:     pub fn take_ring(self) -> RingTransport {
155:         self.ring
156:     }
157: 
158:     /// The ring memory layout (region geometry).
159:     pub fn layout(&self) -> MemoryLayout {
160:         *self.layout_ref()
161:     }
162: 
163:     fn layout_ref(&self) -> &MemoryLayout {
164:         self.ring.layout()
165:     }
166: 
167:     /// The single node without a parent (the root).
168:     pub fn root_id(&self) -> Option<u32> {
169:         self.nodes.values().find(|n| n.parent.is_none()).map(|n| n.id)
170:     }
171: 
172:     /// Materialize a `pathland_view::Node` subtree rooted at `id`.
173:     fn materialize(&self, id: u32) -> Option<Node> {
174:         let flat = self.nodes.get(&id)?.clone();
175:         let mut node = Node::from_component(&flat.view_component);
176:         node.id = flat.id;
177:         node.properties = flat.properties.clone();
178:         for child_id in &flat.children {
179:             if let Some(child) = self.materialize(*child_id) {
180:                 node.children.push(child);
181:             }
182:         }
183:         Some(node)
184:     }
185: }
186: 
187: impl Default for NativeHost {
188:     fn default() -> Self {
189:         Self::new()
190:     }
191: }

193: /// Map a raw u32 component id (C ABI) to a `pathland_view::Component`.

195: /// Mirrors the `component` variant values: hstack=1, vstack=2, text=3,
196: /// button=4, spacer=8.

198:     match id {

200:         x if x == component_type::VSTACK as u32 => Some(pathland_view::Component::VStack),
201:         x if x == component_type::TEXT as u32 => {
202:             Some(pathland_view::Component::Text { text: String::new() })
203:         }
204:         x if x == component_type::BUTTON as u32 => {
205:             Some(pathland_view::Component::Button { label: String::new() })
206:         }
207:         x if x == component_type::SPACER as u32 => Some(pathland_view::Component::Spacer),
208:         _ => None,
209:     }
210: }

224:     ) {
225:         pathland_opcode::value_type::COLOR
226:     } else {
227:         pathland_opcode::value_type::F32

18:  * serialization.

20: public final class RingReader {

22:     // Header field offsets (little-endian), see pathland-opcode::memory.
23:     static final int OFF_RING_OFFSET = 0x06;
24:     static final int OFF_SLOT_COUNT = 0x0E;
25:     static final int OFF_ARENA_OFFSET = 0x12;
26:     static final int OFF_READ_CURSOR = 0x1E;
27:     static final int OFF_WRITE_CURSOR = 0x22;
28: 
29:     // Categories / commands.
30:     static final int CAT_TREE = 0x01;
31:     static final int CAT_STYLE = 0x02;
32:     static final int CMD_SET_TEXT = 0x03;
33: 
34:     private RingReader() {}
35: 
36:     private static int u32(Pointer p, long off) {
37:         // little-endian read
38:         return p.getInt(off);
39:     }
40: 
41:     private static int u16(Pointer p, long off) {
42:         return p.getShort(off) & 0xFFFF;
43:     }
44: 
45:     /** A decoded reference to a tree node's text (from SET_TEXT). */
46:     public static final class TextEntry {
47:         public final int id;
48:         public final String text;
49:         TextEntry(int id, String text) {
50:             this.id = id;
51:             this.text = text;
52:         }
53:     }
54: 
55:     /**
56:      * Read all {@code STYLE:SET_TEXT} entries in the current ring frame,
57:      * zero-copy.
58:      */
59:     public static List<TextEntry> readTextEntries(Pointer mem) {
60:         List<TextEntry> out = new ArrayList<>();
61:         int ringOff = u32(mem, OFF_RING_OFFSET);
62:         int slotCount = u32(mem, OFF_SLOT_COUNT);
63:         int arenaOff = u32(mem, OFF_ARENA_OFFSET);
64:         int readCur = u32(mem, OFF_READ_CURSOR);
65:         int writeCur = u32(mem, OFF_WRITE_CURSOR);
66:         if (slotCount <= 0) {
67:             return out;
68:         }
69:         int mask = slotCount - 1;
70:         int n = writeCur - readCur;
71:         if (n < 0 || n > slotCount) {
72:             n = 0; // wrapped; ignore for the reference demo
73:         }
74:         for (int i = 0; i < n; i++) {
75:             int slot = (readCur + i) & mask;
76:             long base = ringOff + (long) slot * 16;
77:             int cat = mem.getByte(base) & 0xFF;
78:             int cmd = mem.getByte(base + 1) & 0xFF;
79:             int nodeA = u32(mem, base + 4);
80:             int bVal = u32(mem, base + 8);
81:             if (cat == CAT_STYLE && cmd == CMD_SET_TEXT) {
82:                 out.add(new TextEntry(nodeA, readArenaString(mem, arenaOff, bVal)));
83:             }

85:         return out;

1: //! # pathland-host
2: //!
3: //! Host-side reader for the Pathland 16-byte opcode ring. Consumes frames from
4: //! shared linear memory and builds a **native-element description**: the tree
5: //! structure (`TREE`) plus constraint properties (`STYLE`) a renderer maps onto
6: //! that platform's native elements (GTK widgets, DOM elements, HTML).
7: //!
8: //! The engine does not compute layout; this crate stores only what the renderer
9: //! needs to create native elements and let them lay themselves out.
10: 
11: use std::collections::HashMap;
12: 
13: pub use pathland_engine;
14: pub use pathland_opcode;
15: 
16: use pathland_opcode::category;
17: use pathland_opcode::component_type;
18: use pathland_opcode::style;

22: /// A decoded node in the host's native-element description.
23: #[derive(Debug, Clone, PartialEq)]
24: pub struct HostNode {
25:     pub id: u32,
26:     pub component_type: u16,
27:     pub text: Option<String>,
28:     pub parent: Option<u32>,
29:     pub children: Vec<u32>,
30:     /// Constraint properties (propertyId → value) for native layout/styling.
31:     pub properties: HashMap<u16, u32>,
32: }
33: 
34: impl Default for HostNode {
35:     fn default() -> Self {
36:         Self {
37:             id: 0,
38:             component_type: component_type::HSTACK,
39:             text: None,
40:             parent: None,
41:             children: Vec::new(),
42:             properties: HashMap::new(),
43:         }
44:     }
45: }
46: 
47: /// The host's native-element description of a rendered tree.
48: #[derive(Debug, Default)]
49: pub struct RenderTree {
50:     /// nodeId → node.
51:     pub nodes: HashMap<u32, HostNode>,
52: }
53: 
54: impl RenderTree {
55:     /// Apply a frame's opcodes to this tree (a delta).
56:     pub fn apply_frame(&mut self, frame: &Frame<'_>) {
57:         for op in frame.opcodes() {
58:             match (op.category(), op.command()) {
59:                 (category::TREE, tree::CREATE_NODE) => {
60:                     let id = op.a();
61:                     let ty = op.b() as u16;
62:                     let entry = self.nodes.entry(id).or_default();
63:                     entry.id = id;
64:                     entry.component_type = ty;
65:                 }
66:                 (category::TREE, tree::DELETE_NODE) => {
67:                     self.nodes.remove(&op.a());
68:                 }
69:                 (category::TREE, tree::INSERT_CHILD) => {
70:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
71:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
72:                         if !p.children.contains(&child) {
73:                             p.children.push(child);
74:                         }
75:                     }
76:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
77:                         c.parent = Some(parent);
78:                     }
79:                 }
80:                 (category::TREE, tree::REMOVE_CHILD) => {
81:                     let (parent, child) = (op.a(), op.b());
82:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
83:                         p.children.retain(|c| *c != child);
84:                     }
85:                     if let Some(c) = self.nodes.get_mut(&child) {
86:                         c.parent = None;
87:                     }
88:                 }
89:                 (category::TREE, tree::MOVE_CHILD) => {
90:                     let (parent, child, new_index) = (op.a(), op.b(), op.c() as usize);
91:                     if let Some(p) = self.nodes.get_mut(&parent) {
92:                         if let Some(pos) = p.children.iter().position(|c| *c == child) {
93:                             p.children.remove(pos);
94:                         }
95:                         let idx = if new_index == usize::MAX {
96:                             p.children.len()
97:                         } else {
98:                             new_index.min(p.children.len())
99:                         };
100:                         p.children.insert(idx, child);
101:                     }
102:                 }
103:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_PROPERTY) => {
104:                     let prop_id = op.b() as u16;
105:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
106:                         n.properties.insert(prop_id, op.c());
107:                     }
108:                 }
109:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_TEXT) => {
110:                     if let Some(n) = self.nodes.get_mut(&op.a()) {
111:                         n.text = frame.arena_str(op.b()).ok().map(|s| s.to_string());
112:                     }
113:                 }
114:                 (category::STYLE, style::SET_DESIGN_TOKEN) => {
115:                     // Token overrides are handled by the renderer's theme layer.
116:                     let _ = op;
117:                 }
118:                 _ => {}
119:             }
120:         }
121:     }
122: 
123:     /// Look up a node by id.
124:     pub fn node(&self, id: u32) -> Option<&HostNode> {
125:         self.nodes.get(&id)
126:     }
127: 
128:     /// The root node (id 0).
129:     pub fn root(&self) -> Option<&HostNode> {
130:         self.nodes.get(&0)
131:     }
132: }

134: /// Decode a frame into a fresh `RenderTree`.
135: pub fn render_tree_from_frame(frame: &Frame<'_>) -> RenderTree {
136:     let mut tree = RenderTree::default();
137:     tree.apply_frame(frame);
138:     tree
139: }
